weekly.title: The Resurrection
weekly.line: Every Sunday is a little Easter: the day Christ rose from the dead.

psalm.text: This is the day that the Lord has made. We will rejoice and be glad in it!

reading.text: Why do you seek the living among the dead? He isn't here, but is risen.

midday.text: I am the resurrection and the life.

evening.text: You will show me the path of life. In your presence is fullness of joy.

weekly.intention: Where could you bring new life today: a fresh start, a reconciliation, a word of encouragement?

weekly.title: The Angels and the Unseen
weekly.line: The week begins by remembering that we live among more than we can see.

psalm.text: Praise the Lord, all you his angels, who are mighty in strength, who fulfil his word.

reading.text: Don't forget to show hospitality to strangers, for in doing so, some have entertained angels without knowing it.

midday.text: He will put his angels in charge of you, to guard you in all your ways.

evening.text: The angel of the Lord encamps around those who fear him, and delivers them.

weekly.intention: Who is the stranger you could welcome today?

weekly.title: Turning Around
weekly.line: Tuesday remembers John the Baptist, who called people to turn around and start again.

psalm.text: Create in me a clean heart, O God. Renew a right spirit within me.

reading.text: Make ready the way of the Lord! Make his paths straight!

midday.text: In returning and rest you will be saved. In quietness and in confidence will be your strength.

evening.text: As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our transgressions from us.

weekly.intention: What habit or attitude do you want to turn away from, starting today?

weekly.title: Keeping Faith
weekly.line: By tradition Judas agreed to betray Jesus on a Wednesday. Today we pray to be faithful.

psalm.text: His compassion doesn't fail. It is new every morning. Great is your faithfulness.

reading.text: He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much.

midday.text: Where you go, I will go; and where you stay, I will stay.

evening.text: Your loving kindness, Lord, is in the heavens. Your faithfulness reaches to the skies.

weekly.intention: Who is relying on you? Keep one promise to them today, however small.

weekly.title: Friends at the Table
weekly.line: On a Thursday Jesus shared bread with his friends and washed their feet.

psalm.text: See how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to live together in unity!

reading.text: No longer do I call you servants. I have called you friends.

midday.text: Just as I have loved you, you also love one another.

evening.text: You prepare a table before me. My cup runs over.

weekly.intention: Who could you share a meal or a real conversation with this week?

weekly.title: The Cross
weekly.line: Every Friday remembers the day Jesus gave himself for the world.

psalm.text: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?

reading.text: Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends.

midday.text: Father, forgive them, for they don't know what they are doing.

evening.text: He was pierced for our transgressions. He was crushed for our iniquities; by his wounds we are healed.

weekly.intention: Is there someone you need to forgive, even a little, today?

weekly.title: Rest and Remembering
weekly.line: Saturday is the Sabbath, the day of rest, when Christians also remember those who have died.

psalm.text: My soul rests in God alone. My salvation is from him.

reading.text: Come to me, all you who labour and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.

midday.text: Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.

evening.text: He will wipe away every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more.

weekly.intention: Who have you lost? Give thanks for them today, and let yourself rest.

lent.title: Lent: Into the Wilderness
lent.line: For forty days Jesus fasted in the desert. Lent is our forty days.

psalm.text: As the deer pants for the water brooks, so my soul pants after you, God.

reading.text: Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness, and he fasted forty days and forty nights.

midday.text: Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of God's mouth.

evening.text: Search me, God, and know my heart. Lead me in the everlasting way.

lent.intention: What one thing will you give up or take up this week, to make room for God?

lent.title: Lent: Prayer
lent.line: The first of the three Lenten disciplines: prayer.

psalm.text: Let my prayer be set before you like incense.

reading.text: When you pray, enter into your inner room, and having shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret.

midday.text: Be still, and know that I am God.

evening.text: I will lie down in peace and sleep, for you alone, Lord, make me live in safety.

lent.intention: Find five quiet minutes today with no phone, and simply be with God.

lent.title: Lent: Fasting and Simplicity
lent.line: The second discipline: fasting, which makes space for what matters.

psalm.text: Create in me a clean heart, O God.

reading.text: Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of God's mouth.

midday.text: Isn't this the fast that I have chosen: to release the bonds of wickedness, and to let the oppressed go free?

evening.text: My soul thirsts for God, for the living God.

lent.intention: What could you go without today, and give the time or money to someone else?

lent.title: Lent: Generosity
lent.line: The third discipline: giving to those in need, quietly.

psalm.text: Blessed is he who considers the poor.

reading.text: When you do merciful deeds, don't let your left hand know what your right hand does.

midday.text: God loves a cheerful giver.

evening.text: Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good; for his loving kindness endures forever.

lent.intention: Give something away today without telling anyone.

lent.title: Lent: Coming Home
lent.line: The story of the prodigal son: however far we wander, the Father runs to meet us.

psalm.text: Have mercy on me, God, according to your loving kindness.

reading.text: While he was still far off, his father saw him, and was moved with compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.

midday.text: Return to me, and I will return to you.

evening.text: As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our transgressions from us.

lent.intention: Is there a relationship you need to come home to? Take one step.

lent.title: Lent: The Way of the Cross
lent.line: On Fridays in Lent, Christians walk in their minds the road Jesus walked to the cross.

psalm.text: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?

reading.text: He humbled himself, becoming obedient to death, yes, the death of the cross.

midday.text: Father, forgive them, for they don't know what they are doing.

evening.text: By his wounds we are healed.

lent.intention: Carry someone else's burden today: a chore, a worry, a hard conversation.

lent.title: Lent: Waiting
lent.line: Lent teaches us to wait, and to trust in the dark.

psalm.text: I wait for the Lord. My soul waits. I hope in his word.

reading.text: It is good that a man should hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the Lord.

midday.text: Wait for the Lord. Be strong, and let your heart take courage.

evening.text: Into your hands I commend my spirit.

lent.intention: What are you waiting for in your life? Hand it to God tonight.

advent.title: Advent: Hope
advent.line: The first week of Advent: in the darkest time of the year, we wait for the light.

psalm.text: I wait for the Lord. My soul waits. I hope in his word.

reading.text: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light.

midday.text: May the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing.

evening.text: Guide me in your truth, and teach me, for you are the God of my salvation.

advent.intention: Where do you need hope? Bring a little of it to someone else today.

advent.title: Advent: Peace
advent.line: The second week of Advent: waiting for the Prince of Peace.

psalm.text: Mercy and truth meet together. Righteousness and peace have kissed each other.

reading.text: For to us a child is born. His name shall be called Wonderful Counsellor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

midday.text: Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you.

evening.text: They shall beat their swords into ploughshares.

advent.intention: Where could you make peace this week: at home, at work, in yourself?

advent.title: Advent: Joy
advent.line: The third week of Advent, traditionally called Gaudete: Rejoice!

psalm.text: The Lord has done great things for us, and we are glad.

reading.text: My soul magnifies the Lord. My spirit has rejoiced in God my Saviour.

midday.text: Rejoice in the Lord always! Again I will say, Rejoice!

evening.text: The desert shall rejoice and blossom like a rose.

advent.intention: Notice three joys today, and share one of them.

advent.title: Advent: Love
advent.line: The last week of Advent: Mary says yes, and love comes into the world.

psalm.text: Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good; for his loving kindness endures forever.

reading.text: Behold, the servant of the Lord; let it be done to me according to your word.

midday.text: We love, because he first loved us.

evening.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his one and only Son.

advent.intention: Who needs to feel loved before Christmas? Tell them.

christmastide.title: Christmastide: God With Us
christmastide.line: The twelve days of Christmas: God has come to live among us.

psalm.text: Sing to the Lord a new song, for he has done marvellous things!

reading.text: The Word became flesh, and lived among us. We saw his glory.

midday.text: They shall call his name Immanuel, which means, God with us.

evening.text: Make a joyful noise to the Lord, all the earth!

christmastide.intention: Who could use a visit or a call during these twelve days?

holyweek.title: Holy Week
holyweek.line: The last week of Jesus' life, as he walks towards the cross.

psalm.text: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?

reading.text: When he came near, he saw the city and wept over it.

midday.text: Not my will, but yours, be done.

evening.text: Into your hands I commend my spirit.

holyweek.intention: Stay close to someone who is suffering this week.

ash-wednesday.title: Ash Wednesday
ash-wednesday.line: Lent begins. "Remember that you are dust, and to dust you shall return."

psalm.text: Have mercy on me, God, according to your loving kindness. Create in me a clean heart.

reading.text: Tear your heart and not your garments, and turn to the Lord your God; for he is gracious and merciful.

midday.text: For you are dust, and to dust you shall return.

evening.text: As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our transgressions from us.

ash-wednesday.intention: Choose your Lent: one thing to give up, one thing to take up, one person to give to.

palm-sunday.title: Palm Sunday
palm-sunday.line: Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a donkey, and the crowds wave palms.

psalm.text: Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!

reading.text: Hosanna to the son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!

midday.text: Your King comes to you, humble, and riding on a donkey.

evening.text: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?

palm-sunday.intention: Welcome Jesus into the week ahead: what would you like him to find?

maundy-thursday.title: Maundy Thursday
maundy-thursday.line: The Last Supper, when Jesus washed his friends' feet and gave the new commandment: love one another.

psalm.text: What will I give to the Lord for all his benefits toward me? I will take the cup of salvation.

reading.text: If I then, the Lord and the Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet.

midday.text: A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another.

evening.text: Not my will, but yours, be done.

maundy-thursday.intention: Do one humble, hidden act of service for someone today.

good-friday.title: Good Friday
good-friday.line: The day Jesus died on the cross. Christians call it good, because of what it won.

psalm.text: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?

reading.text: He was pierced for our transgressions. He was crushed for our iniquities. The punishment that brought our peace was on him; and by his wounds we are healed.

midday.text: It is finished.

evening.text: Father, into your hands I commit my spirit!

good-friday.intention: Keep an hour of quiet today, perhaps between noon and three, when Jesus hung on the cross.

holy-saturday.title: Holy Saturday
holy-saturday.line: The day of silence, when Jesus lay in the tomb and the world waited.

psalm.text: I wait for the Lord. My soul waits. I hope in his word.

reading.text: Joseph took the body, wrapped it in a clean linen cloth, and laid it in his own new tomb.

midday.text: It is good that a man should hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the Lord.

evening.text: In peace I will both lay myself down and sleep.

holy-saturday.intention: Sit with the silence today. Grief and waiting are part of faith too.

easter.title: Easter Day
easter.line: Christ is risen! The heart of the Christian faith.

psalm.text: This is the day that the Lord has made. We will rejoice and be glad in it!

reading.text: He is not here, for he has risen, just like he said.

midday.text: Death, where is your sting? Hades, where is your victory?

evening.text: I am the resurrection and the life.

easter.intention: Share the joy: send an Easter greeting to someone you haven't spoken to in a while.

ascension.title: Ascension Day
ascension.line: Forty days after Easter, Jesus returns to the Father, promising to be with us always.

psalm.text: God has gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet.

reading.text: While they were looking, he was taken up, and a cloud received him out of their sight.

midday.text: I am with you always, even to the end of the age.

evening.text: You will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses.

ascension.intention: Jesus sent his friends out. Where are you being sent?

pentecost.title: Pentecost
pentecost.line: The Holy Spirit comes like wind and fire, and the Church is born.

psalm.text: You send out your Spirit and they are created. You renew the face of the ground.

reading.text: Suddenly there came from the sky a sound like the rushing of a mighty wind, and tongues like fire appeared, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit.

midday.text: The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith, gentleness, and self-control.

evening.text: Come, Holy Spirit.

pentecost.intention: Pick one fruit of the Spirit to practise today: patience, kindness or gentleness.

trinity.title: Trinity Sunday
trinity.line: One God in three persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit, a communion of love.

psalm.text: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God, the Almighty.

reading.text: Go and make disciples of all nations, baptising them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.

midday.text: God is love.

evening.text: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, God's love, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all.

trinity.intention: God is a relationship of love. Invest in one of yours today.

01-01.title: New Year: The Naming of Jesus
01-01.line: A new year, and the day Jesus was named. His name means 'God saves'.

psalm.text: So teach us to count our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.

reading.text: You shall call his name Jesus, for it is he who shall save his people from their sins.

midday.text: Behold, I am making all things new.

evening.text: His compassion doesn't fail. It is new every morning. Great is your faithfulness.

01-01.intention: Instead of a resolution, choose one way to build something good this year.

01-06.title: The Epiphany
01-06.line: The wise men follow a star and find the Christ child: God revealed to the whole world.

psalm.text: Arise, shine; for your light has come, and the Lord's glory has risen on you.

reading.text: When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceedingly great joy. They offered him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.

midday.text: I am the light of the world.

evening.text: The heavens declare the glory of God.

01-06.intention: The wise men followed a star. What is drawing you towards God?

02-02.title: Candlemas
02-02.line: Forty days after Christmas, the baby Jesus is presented in the Temple, and old Simeon sees the light of the world.

psalm.text: The Lord is my light and my salvation.

reading.text: Now you are releasing your servant, Master, in peace; for my eyes have seen your salvation, a light for revelation to the nations.

midday.text: The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness hasn't overcome it.

evening.text: In your light we will see light.

02-02.intention: Light a candle today, and pray for someone who is in a dark place.

03-17.title: St Patrick
03-17.line: The patron saint of Ireland, once a slave there, who went back to bring the gospel.

psalm.text: The Lord is my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer.

reading.text: Christ with me, Christ before me, Christ behind me, Christ in me, Christ beneath me, Christ above me.

midday.text: Go and make disciples of all nations.

evening.text: I will both lay myself down in peace and sleep.

03-17.intention: Patrick returned to the people who had enslaved him. Who could you show unexpected grace to?

03-25.title: The Annunciation
03-25.line: The angel Gabriel visits Mary, and she says yes to God.

psalm.text: My soul magnifies the Lord.

reading.text: Behold, the servant of the Lord; let it be done to me according to your word.

midday.text: For nothing spoken by God is impossible.

evening.text: The Word became flesh, and lived among us.

03-25.intention: What is God asking you to say yes to?

06-09.title: St Columba
06-09.line: The Irish monk who founded the monastery on Iona in 563 and brought the gospel to Scotland.

psalm.text: The earth is the Lord's, with its fullness.

reading.text: Go into all the world, and preach the Good News to the whole creation.

midday.text: How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news.

evening.text: The Lord will keep your going out and your coming in.

06-09.intention: Columba made a small island a light to a nation. Where is your 'Iona', the place you could shine?

06-24.title: The Birth of John the Baptist
06-24.line: The forerunner, who pointed away from himself to Jesus.

psalm.text: Create in me a clean heart, O God.

reading.text: He must increase, but I must decrease.

midday.text: Make ready the way of the Lord!

evening.text: You, child, will be called a prophet of the Most High.

06-24.intention: Point attention away from yourself today: praise someone else's work.

06-29.title: Saints Peter and Paul
06-29.line: The fisherman and the former persecutor: two very different men, both martyrs in Rome.

psalm.text: Their voice has gone out through all the earth.

reading.text: I have fought the good fight. I have finished the course. I have kept the faith.

midday.text: You are Peter, and on this rock I will build my assembly.

evening.text: My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.

06-29.intention: Peter failed and was restored; Paul was turned around. Who deserves a second chance from you?

07-22.title: St Mary Magdalene
07-22.line: The first witness of the resurrection, called the apostle to the apostles.

psalm.text: My soul thirsts for you, my flesh longs for you.

reading.text: Jesus said to her, "Mary." She turned and said to him, "Rabboni!" which is to say, "Teacher!"

midday.text: I have seen the Lord!

evening.text: Weeping may stay for the night, but joy comes in the morning.

07-22.intention: Jesus called her by name. Who could you notice and call by name today?

08-06.title: The Transfiguration
08-06.line: On a mountain, Jesus' friends see him shining with the glory of God.

psalm.text: In your light we will see light.

reading.text: His face shone like the sun, and his garments became as white as the light.

midday.text: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to him.

evening.text: The heavens declare the glory of God.

08-06.intention: Look for a moment of glory today: in nature, music or a face.

09-29.title: Michaelmas: St Michael and All Angels
09-29.line: The feast of the archangels and the battle of good against evil.

psalm.text: Praise the Lord, all you his angels, who are mighty in strength.

reading.text: There was war in the sky. Michael and his angels made war on the dragon.

midday.text: He will put his angels in charge of you, to guard you in all your ways.

evening.text: The angel of the Lord encamps around those who fear him, and delivers them.

09-29.intention: Stand up for what is good in one small, concrete way today.

10-02.title: The Guardian Angels
10-02.line: An old tradition says every person, especially every child, is watched over by an angel.

psalm.text: He will put his angels in charge of you, to guard you in all your ways.

reading.text: See that you don't despise one of these little ones, for in heaven their angels always see the face of my Father.

midday.text: The angel of the Lord encamps around those who fear him, and delivers them.

evening.text: In peace I will both lay myself down and sleep, for you alone, Lord, make me live in safety.

10-02.intention: Be a guardian for someone today: look out for a child, a neighbour or a colleague.

10-04.title: St Francis of Assisi
10-04.line: The rich young man who gave everything away, loved the poor and called the sun his brother.

psalm.text: The earth is the Lord's, with its fullness.

reading.text: Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow. Even Solomon in all his glory was not dressed like one of these.

midday.text: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.

evening.text: Let everything that has breath praise the Lord!

10-04.intention: Spend ten minutes outside today, and give thanks for one living thing.

11-01.title: All Saints
11-01.line: The great company of holy men and women, known and unknown, who have gone before us.

psalm.text: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints.

reading.text: Since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us run with perseverance the race that is set before us.

midday.text: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.

evening.text: He will wipe away every tear from their eyes.

11-01.intention: Who has shown you what goodness looks like? Thank them, or thank God for them.

11-02.title: All Souls
11-02.line: A day to remember and pray for all who have died.

psalm.text: Out of the depths I have cried to you, Lord.

reading.text: In my Father's house are many homes. I am going to prepare a place for you.

midday.text: I am the resurrection and the life.

evening.text: He will wipe away every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more.

11-02.intention: Say the names of those you have lost, aloud, and give thanks for them.

11-11.title: Remembrance
11-11.line: We remember those who died in war, and pray for peace.

psalm.text: He makes wars cease to the end of the earth.

reading.text: Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends.

midday.text: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God.

evening.text: They shall beat their swords into ploughshares.

11-11.intention: Keep the two minutes' silence at 11:00, and pray for a place at war today.

11-16.title: St Margaret of Scotland
11-16.line: The 11th-century queen who fed the poor at her own table and built a ferry for pilgrims.

psalm.text: Blessed is he who considers the poor.

reading.text: I was hungry, and you gave me food to eat. I was a stranger, and you took me in.

midday.text: Inasmuch as you did it to one of the least of these, you did it to me.

evening.text: Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good.

11-16.intention: Feed someone today: buy a coffee, give to a food bank, invite someone in.

11-30.title: St Andrew
11-30.line: Patron saint of Scotland, the fisherman who brought his brother to Jesus.

psalm.text: Come, see the works of God.

reading.text: He first found his own brother, Simon, and said to him, "We have found the Messiah!" He brought him to Jesus.

midday.text: Come after me, and I will make you fishers for people.

evening.text: How beautiful are the feet of those who preach the Good News of peace.

11-30.intention: Andrew brought his brother. Who could you invite: to a meal, a conversation, or church?

12-06.title: St Nicholas
12-06.line: The 4th-century bishop who gave secret gifts to the poor, the real Santa Claus.

psalm.text: Blessed is he who considers the poor.

reading.text: When you do merciful deeds, don't let your left hand know what your right hand does.

midday.text: It is more blessed to give than to receive.

evening.text: God loves a cheerful giver.

12-06.intention: Give a secret gift today, and tell your children the real story of St Nicholas.

12-24.title: Christmas Eve
12-24.line: The holy night: waiting at the manger.

psalm.text: The heavens declare the glory of God.

reading.text: She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth, and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.

midday.text: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light.

evening.text: Glory to God in the highest, on earth peace, good will toward men.

12-24.intention: Make room tonight: for God, and for anyone without a place to go.

12-25.title: Christmas Day
12-25.line: God becomes a child. The Word becomes flesh.

psalm.text: Sing to the Lord a new song, for he has done marvellous things!

reading.text: I bring you good news of great joy which will be to all the people. For there is born to you today a Saviour, who is Christ the Lord.

midday.text: The Word became flesh, and lived among us.

evening.text: Glory to God in the highest, on earth peace.

12-25.intention: Who is alone this Christmas? Reach out to them today.

12-26.title: St Stephen
12-26.line: The first Christian martyr, who forgave those who killed him. Good King Wenceslas went out on this day to help the poor.

psalm.text: Into your hands I commend my spirit.

reading.text: Lord Jesus, receive my spirit! Lord, don't hold this sin against them!

midday.text: Love your enemies, and pray for those who persecute you.

evening.text: It is more blessed to give than to receive.

12-26.intention: Like Wenceslas, take something to someone in need today.

easterweek.title: Easter Week: Christ Is Risen
easterweek.line: The week after Easter is one long celebration: the tomb is empty and everything has changed.

psalm.text: This is the day that the Lord has made. We will rejoice and be glad in it!

reading.text: Jesus himself came near, and went with them. Their eyes were opened, and they recognised him.

midday.text: Peace be to you.

evening.text: Stay with us, for it is almost evening, and the day is almost over.

easterweek.intention: The risen Jesus walked with two sad friends. Walk alongside someone who is struggling today.
